title: Router: parameters, child routes, resolvers and redirects

videos.script:
Until now the planner drew both screens on one page, with the course fixed in the code. This lesson gives every screen an address, so a link, a bookmark and the back button all work.

{{routes}} Routes map an address to a component, and the router draws it where the application has an outlet. The order of the routes is part of what they mean.

{{links}} Router links change the screen without reloading the page, and the current one is marked for a screen reader. The tests notice the router, and you give them one.

{{params}} A route parameter arrives as the same input the course page already had.

{{children}} Child routes split the course page in two: its sessions, and the form, each at an address of its own.

{{redirects}} Redirects keep old addresses working.

{{titles}} And every page gets a title, the first thing a screen reader says after a navigation, with a resolver for the one that needs the data.
